title: Structure Is Not Security: Poisoning Graph-Based Agent Memory Through the Extraction Pipeline
description: Knowledge graphs are becoming the memory layer of AI agents — text promoted into typed, embedded, retrievable nodes the agent later trusts. Their promise is structure: schema, typing, ontology validation. This talk argues that the structure is the attack surface, and that the layer where defenses usually live — the database — is the wrong place to look. Using a reproducible proof-of-concept against a graph-backed agent memory system, I trace a kill chain that ends with an agent acting on attacker-controlled "knowledge," and threat-model why structural validation gives false assurance and where defense actually has to move. If you build or deploy graph-backed AI, you'll leave with a threat model you didn't have.

title: Merging Under Load: Point-in-Time Entity Resolution on a Live Neo4j Graph
description: Entity resolution looks like data cleaning: cluster the duplicates, elect a canonical, merge, keep an audit trail. This usually works - until the graph is read every second by AML rules, sanctions screening, and analysts on open cases. Thus it's not data cleaning, it's a concurrency problem. And Neo4j doesn't give you point-in-time consistency for free. You build it yourself, in Cypher. Sunidhi grounds this in TerraLens, a transaction monitoring and screening engine for a large regulated financial services provider: nearly 60 million transaction relationships, growing by the second, re-resolved every hour while live services read and write it. Every obvious escape is closed. You can't pause the graph. You can't rebuild from scratch, it takes hours and erases merge history regulators can demand. You can't destructively merge an entity someone may be mid-investigation on. Something is always mid-read, so the merge has to land under live queries without them noticing. What you'll take away: treat a merge as a concurrent mutation, not a batch edit; hold a consistent point-in-time view for a reader while the entity it's reading is merged away; make the merge status-aware, so a node under investigation is handled differently from a settled one; mutate a heavily-read graph on a schedule while keeping a durable, queryable audit trail. Sunidhi will be candid about what the design leaves to human review, and where it stops.

title: Microsoft Fabric Workload: Return to Lakehouse
description: Neo4j’s integration with Microsoft Fabric keeps evolving. With our Workload offering you can bring your Lakehouse data into Neo4j. Run graph analytics over your graph. Finally, in our newest feature, you can now write your analytics data from Neo4j back to Lakehouse. In this NODES presentation you will be shown a demo use end-to-end use case on how you can use Neo4j and Microsoft Fabric together to its maximum capacity.

title: Neo4j Spark Connector Meets Spark 4
description: Neo4j Spark Connector v6 is a major new release that adds official support for Apache Spark 4.0 and 4.1 while modernizing the connector’s technical foundation. The new version also expands the Cypher capabilities available through the connector, including support for query tuning preambles, runtime selection, parallel runtimes, and Cypher 25 features. These additions give Spark users more control over how their queries are executed and access to the latest capabilities of Neo4j. This session will introduce and demonstrate the key changes in the release. Attendees will learn what is new in version 6, why these changes matter, and how the connector makes it possible to take advantage of modern Spark and Cypher features when working with Neo4j.

title: Neo4j Kafka Connector 6: A Major Step Forward
description: Neo4j Kafka Connector 6 is a major new release focused on modernizing the connector’s foundation while improving the developer experience for streaming data into/out of Neo4j. V6 brings significant under-the-hood renovations, including support for the latest Neo4j driver. This session will introduce the key changes in the release, including a unified schema model for nodes and relationships, improved database constraint management, exactly-once semantics, and quality-of-life enhancements such as support for Kafka metrics plugins. Attendees will learn what has changed in version 6, why these changes matter, and how the new release makes it easier to build, operate, and observe Kafka-based data pipelines with Neo4j.

title: The Neo4j Aura Terraform Provider: Infrastructure as Code for Aura
description: Terraform has become one of the most widely adopted tools for Infrastructure as Code, enabling teams to manage cloud resources through declarative configuration and automated workflows. But what does it take to expose a cloud platform through Terraform? This session explores the Neo4j Aura Terraform Provider and how Terraform can be used to manage Neo4j Aura resources in a repeatable and automated way. We'll discuss the motivation behind this approach, examine the architecture and design of a Terraform provider, demonstrate the Neo4j Aura Terraform Provider in action, and explore potential future directions for Infrastructure as Code within the Neo4j ecosystem.

title: Graph Types: Schema Enforcement Made Easy
description: The schemaless nature of graph databases is a superpower: iterate fast, evolve your model freely, get data in without ceremony. But production systems need data integrity, and AI agents need to know what your graph actually looks like. Without a declared schema,both become hard problems. GRAPH TYPE is Neo4j's answer. Now generally available, it lets you declare your entire data model in a single, readable statement — nodes, properties, types, label implications, and relationship constraints all in one place. One declaration replaces a dozen scattered commands. One source of truth for your schema. In this session we'll explore how GRAPH TYPE works, manage it through its lifecycle (SET, ADD, ALTER, DROP), and enforce data integrity from day one. We'll demo it live and show what happens when the data doesn't fit. We'll also cover a use case that's become essential: schema discovery. SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE gives agents a clean, structured picture of your graph — no more guessing schema from sample data. Finally, we're not done yet. We'll talk about what's next on the roadmap for schema in Neo4j. Leave knowing what GRAPH TYPE can do today, how to adopt it, and where it's heading.

title: A Murder of MCP Servers: Taming AI Tool Sprawl with GraphQL Federation and a Knowledge Graph
description: MCP solved the AI integration problem. Every SaaS vendor ships a server now. Wire several together and you get a different problem: auth sprawl, disconnected tool namespaces, and response shapes each agent handles. The constraint in production AI isn't connecting to systems; it's managing the surface area. GraphQL federation resolved this for REST — independent services behind a single unified schema. The same pattern can applies to MCP server sprawl. Platform vendors are already shipping production gateways that prove it. This session shows how, from three real systems — Neo4j, Linear, and Slack — we build a federation gateway exposing all three as a single MCP endpoint. We cover subgraph configuration, persisted operations that govern what an agent can call, and the graph data model that connects the systems. The second half shows what a knowledge graph adds. Neo4j isn't a third data source here — it's the layer that holds the relationships between the other two. We model Linear issues and Slack threads as nodes, connect them with typed edges, and write the Cypher that makes cross-system reasoning possible. The closing demo traverses all three as a connected graph: one auth token, one log entry, one answer none of them could produce alone. A federated endpoint is manageable. A knowledge graph makes it intelligent. Code and data model on GitHub before the conference.

title: Going Full Circle with Virtual Graphs and Relational Databases
description: Many years ago I gave presentations based on my work on Spring Data Neo4j: Going from relational databases to databases with relations. Back then I had to choose: Having data in both relational databases and import them into a Graph database for more insights. WIth Neo4j announcing Virtual Graphs in the summer of 2026, I do no longer have to chose: I can connect Neo4j to any relational databases and query my tables like I would query a graph. In this session I pick up my favourite topic doing database presentations: Musical habits and statistics. I will demonstrate kind of a medallion architecture, in which a relational database receives raw listening data (scrobbels), basically the bronze level, and how it can aggregate it into silver level and eventually, connect Neo4j Virtual Graph to that dataset and create gold level value by connecting aggregated data with context only a graph can produce.

title: Graph Analytics for Every Builder: What's New, What's Possible, and What's Next
description: Graph Analytics has a reputation for being the domain of data scientists and algorithm experts, but that story is changing fast. In this session, you'll discover how Graph Analytics is becoming accessible to the full spectrum of Neo4j users and beyond, from analysts to app developers to ML practitioners. The session will cover the expanding use case landscape and how getting started with Graph Analytics has never been easier — whether you're building traditional analytics pipelines or AI-powered applications via MCP, agent skills, and Aura-native integrations. You'll then learn about the new capabilities of Aura Graph Analytics (deeper Python ecosystem integration, new algorithms, ML model persistence, async execution, and more), and how the Graph Analytics offering is evolving for self-managed customers. The session will end with a look at what's coming next that will change the scale at which graph analytics runs.

title: Vercel SDK Integration with Neo4j
description: LLM-powered chat applications are traditionally stateless, often suffering from "amnesia" that forces them to re-derive context, leading to expensive and inefficient prompt-stuffing. This presentation explores a production-ready solution: integrating the Neo4j Agent Memory System (NAMS) with the Vercel AI SDK. We will walk through the implementation of a persistent memory layer that categorizes knowledge into short-term, long-term, and reasoning graph structures. I will demonstrate two distinct integration patterns: Provider Mode: A transparent middleware approach for seamless, "invisible" memory integration. Tools Mode: A model-driven approach that grants the agent agency over memory, providing auditability and debuggability. We will also cover best practices for using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to bridge conversational memory with live graph data and discuss strategies for optimising token usage and memory retrieval latency.

title: Neo4j Product Vision & Roadmap
description: An insider look at the latest Neo4j innovations enabling relationship-driven intelligence at scale. Learn about new features and enhancements that make Neo4j essential for developers building interconnected data apps and AI.

title: Aura Agent in Production: New Features and Customer Stories
description: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototypes to production, but building agents that can reason over enterprise data and deliver real business value remains a challenge. In this session, you'll discover the latest innovations in Neo4j Aura Agent and hear directly from customers who are deploying graph-powered agents in production today. We'll start with an overview of the latest Aura Agent capabilities, including the features that help developers build, evaluate, and deploy agents grounded in enterprise knowledge graphs faster than ever. You'll then hear from two customers applying Aura Agent to complex enterprise use cases. AVA (AI Veterans Assistance) uses Neo4j Aura to connect U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations (38 CFR), clinical evidence from medical records, and military service history in a knowledge graph. By connecting these different sources of information, AVA helps veterans assess their potential eligibility for VA disability benefits, understand how their medical and service records support a claim, identify missing evidence, and organize their records against the relevant regulatory requirements. Tokio Marine HCC International will share how they are using knowledge graphs and Aura Agent to analyze complex contract data and uncover cost-saving opportunities. By connecting vendors, locations, services, pricing, and contracts in a graph, analysis of the first 20 contracts identified significant potential savings. They’ll also show how they are using Snowflake Cortex, Aura Agent and Neo4j MCP Server into a broader multi-agent architecture for answering complex business questions. Join us to learn how organizations across industries are using Neo4j Aura Agent to build intelligent, context-aware applications that go beyond chatbots and deliver real business outcomes. What you'll learn: - Explore the latest capabilities and features in Neo4j Aura Agent. - Learn how customers are deploying graph-powered AI agents in production. - Understand the architectural patterns, challenges, and lessons learned from real-world implementations. - Get inspired by practical use cases from healthcare and other industries.
useCases: AI Agents;Artificial Intelligence & Analytics;Data Privacy;Financial Services;GenAI Applications;Government;Life Sciences;Risk & Compliance

title: Fireside Chat with Andrew Ng and Emil Eifrém
description: Building complex agentic systems requires more than connecting AI models—it takes new approaches to engineering, context, and data. In this fireside chat, Dr. Andrew Ng, a global leader in AI innovation and education, joins Emil Eifrem, CEO and Co-Founder of Neo4j, to explore what’s next for AI engineering. They’ll discuss the AI engineering skills map and approaches AI engineers need to build smarter, more capable AI applications.

title: Drivers End-to-End Property Encryption
description: This session introduces Property Encryption, a new feature in Neo4j Drivers that enables end-to-end encryption of Neo4j properties. We’ll explore how it works, how it helps protect sensitive data, and how it can be used in applications that require an additional layer of data confidentiality.

title: Document Intelligence: Agentic Workflows for Knowledge Graphs Speakers
description: urning documents into a useful knowledge graph requires a coherent extraction model, consistent entity identities and links to supporting source passages. An agentic experience brings these operations into a workflow you can guide and inspect. Firat Tekiner and Estelle Scifo will demonstrate how the Document Intelligence agent in Neo4j Aura uses tools to inspect sampled documents, propose and refine graph models, assess their fit for business questions, start imports and retrieve job status. You will see how conversation, canvas editing and extraction previews work together to give you control over the process. They will explain the data engineering behind this experience, from parsing text, images and tables to chunking, embeddings, model-guided extraction and background import. Entity resolution will be a central focus. You will see how the pipeline normalizes names, compares candidate matches and resolves repeated mentions across documents and against existing Aura nodes. They will discuss how duplicate entities and incorrect merges affect downstream queries. Using Cypher and vector search, they will query the connected entity and lexical layers to retrieve facts and supporting passages for downstream AI agents. You will learn how to guide the agent, design the extraction model, inspect entity matches and preserve source provenance when enriching an existing knowledge graph.
useCases: AI Agents;Artificial Intelligence & Analytics;GenAI Applications;General;Knowledge Graph

title: Transit Routing with Jev and Neo4j: A Typed Decision Model in the Graph
description: Language models are good at writing text, but many applications don't need text. They need a decision: take this branch or that one, approve or escalate, route here or there. Jev, a System One model, answers a question with a typed choice and a probability for every option, so you can see how sure the model is and not only what it said. City transit is a natural fit. When stations close or delays build, a rider or an operations team has to choose between routes and a wrong call is costly. We use one such decision from the London Underground Northern line, which branch to take when stations are suspended or delayed, as a worked example of a pattern that applies to any transit network and show it two ways. First from Python, in a few lines of code. Then inside Neo4j, where the state comes from the graph, the decision is a single Cypher call and the same graph finds the way around. You’ll see the same call run against a hosted model and a small local one, and what to do when the network is gone. Key takeaways - A decision that comes with probabilities and a margin is easier to trust, test and escalate than free text. - The same pattern works for any transit network that can be described as a graph. - A hosted model and a small local model can answer the same question through the same call. - Putting the decision next to the data, in the graph, removes a layer of glue code.

title: Typed Decisions in Graphland: New Best Practices from 58+ Experiments
description: Most graph pipelines still make their judgment calls with uncalibrated scores. Drawing on 58 reproducible experiments, Jim Thornton will show how to go from a hand-tuned if score > 0.85: merge to answering those calls (should these two nodes merge, should this extracted fact be written, is this edge still true, which neighbor leads to the goal) with small typed decision models: models that return a probability for a fixed set of options in one forward pass. You will see the pattern behind the wins: Cypher proposes candidates, the model decides, and the probability is stored on the edge so you can set review bands, audit and roll back. Jim will show the Cypher, the exact questions asked and the results: duplicate CRM companies decided correctly 96 times in 100 versus 62 for merging on name, 89 of 100 junk writes from an LLM extractor caught versus 5 for a schema check, and graph walks that reach 18 of 40 targets versus 4 to 7 for an LLM writing Cypher at each hop, for about 4 cents per 1,000 decisions. Just as useful are the ideas that failed, and Jim will cover those too, along with when a plain classifier is enough and an exact, server-free layer that answers lookups straight from Neo4j's store files. You will leave with a strong sense of how best practices for entity resolution, ingestion, graph maintenance and GraphRAG are quickly changing with experiments you can rerun.

title: Native Ontology Management in Neo4j
description: Neo4j is introducing native ontology management to support agentic AI architectures. In this session, we will introduce the new formal Ontology Graph Specification that you can use to create and work with ontologies in Neo4j. You will learn how we plan to persist ontologies, use them to enforce the graph schema, and manage them. We will also explore upcoming Aura tooling for visualizing and sharing ontologies. Join us to see how these new database-level primitives can help your agents reason about your data and bring better accuracy to your agentic GraphRAG workflows.

title: GraphRAG for Good: Context-Aware AI for Women’s Safety and Financial Freedom
description: What does it take to build an AI system that truly understands the complex, interconnected realities of the people it is meant to help? When supporting women escaping domestic abuse, standard AI responses fall short—context, safety, and nuanced relational understanding are critical to guiding survivors toward long-term financial independence. In this session, explore how the non-profit Creating Wings is leveraging Neo4j and GraphRAG (Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to build a deeply context-aware conversational AI agent. Moving beyond basic query-answering, this system connects multi-dimensional data—from immediate safety planning to sustainable career and financial pathways—into a unified knowledge graph that models real-world human needs. Part real-world case study and part technical deep dive, this talk highlights how combining graph databases with generative AI enables technology with true purpose. Attendees will learn practical architectural patterns for context-aware AI and discover how thoughtful engineering can create tangible pathways to safety, opportunity, and freedom.

title: Bringing Neo4j into Laravel
description: In this talk, you'll learn how to integrate Neo4j into your Laravel applications using familiar tools like Eloquent and the Query Builder. We'll introduce Neo4j Laravel, a new open-source package that brings graph database capabilities directly into the Laravel ecosystem. We'll explore how to model highly connected data, work with first-class graph relationships, and use graph databases without sacrificing the Laravel development experience. Through practical examples, we'll demonstrate how to get started and build graph-powered applications using the tools you already know.
